answer: Men and women are essentially the same in every way; any observed differences are largely psychological only. Because both sexes sit on some parts of the body and reproduce the same way, there’s no real point making big assumptions about what each should be doing. Historically, men took the decision-making roles because they were physically stronger and women cooked, cleaned, and clothed them, but with modern birth control, that physical advantage is gone so everyone approaches work and home duties pretty much equally. Inexpert studies show the average man works fewer hours than the average woman, so moving people into “equal” roles is straightforward. For that reason, the ideal goal is to have a completely gender-free workforce where men and women alternate jobs randomly and none of the disparities exist; all else is a leftover social convention that hasn’t shown to have real significance.
